comments.content: The new comment's guarantee does not hold: `updateAppVersion` is reached before an install is confirmed, not only after the older build is on the device. `DetailsViewModel.saveInstalledAppToDatabase` calls `installationManager.updateInstalledAppVersion(...)` with `isPendingInstall = true` whenever `installOutcome != InstallOutcome.COMPLETED` (DetailsViewModel.kt:2104), and on Android `AndroidInstaller.install` always returns `DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM` (AndroidInstaller.kt:113) — it just launches the system installer, which the user can still cancel. So every Android downgrade rewrites the record (and now persists `skippedReleaseTag`) as soon as the installer is launched, which is exactly the situation the deleted `installOutcome == InstallOutcome.COMPLETED` guard in `DetailsViewModel` was there to prevent. The result is that a cancelled downgrade leaves `skippedReleaseTag = latestVersion`, so `checkForUpdates` reports `matchesSkipped` (line 342) and the newer release stays hidden until a strictly newer one appears. Either gate this write on a confirmed install, or clear the skip when a pending install turns out not to have landed (e.g. in `PackageEventReceiver`'s "replaced but not updated to target" branch).

"`updateAppVersion` is also called before the install is confirmed: `DetailsViewModel.saveInstalledAppToDatabase` passes `isPendingInstall = true` whenever `installOutcome != InstallOutcome.COMPLETED`, and on Android `AndroidInstaller.install` always returns `DELEGATED_TO_SYSTEM`, so every Android install (the downgrade path included) rewrites the record as soon as the system installer is launched — the user can still cancel there. The comment's guarantee ("only happens once the older build is actually on the device — an attempt that fails or is cancelled never gets here") therefore does not hold, and the previous code deliberately gated this write on `installOutcome == InstallOutcome.COMPLETED`. As written, a cancelled downgrade leaves `skippedReleaseTag = latestVersion`, which `checkForUpdates` then treats as `matchesSkipped`, hiding the newer release until a strictly newer one appears. Either gate the skip write on a confirmed install or roll it back when a pending install is not confirmed (e.g. PackageEventReceiver's 'replaced but not updated to target' branch)."
